## Summary

A harness pattern for long autonomous runs: before letting a capable model (their example: "Opus 5.5") loose on a long task, have it **vibe-code a quick HTML dashboard for the task first** — presumably live status, progress, intermediate results rendered as a local page. Then institutionalize the skill: a **dedicated subagent that only builds dashboards** ("name it dashboard-builder, set its effort to medium"), so every long task gets an observability surface for near-free.

## Why it matters

- **Observability for agent runs is usually an afterthought; this makes it step zero.** Our own stall (Sep 20–30: routines triggered, nothing visibly ran, nobody noticed for ten days) is the exact failure class this pattern attacks — a dashboard of "last enqueue time / last disposition per agent" would have surfaced the stall on day one. The lesson lands close to home this week.
- **Subagent-as-skill is the reusable move.** Extracting "build me a status page" into a named, medium-effort subagent mirrors [[2026-09-17-agrawal-agent-simplification-prompts]] — spend capability where it pays, package the routine part. It also matches how we run relays: dedicated dumb processes for mechanical jobs.
- **Cheap renderings beat log-diving.** A static HTML page the lead agent rewrites each pass is simpler than any metrics stack — no server, no dependency, and the user can open it in a browser without touching logs. Same philosophy as our relay `tick ok` logs, but human-readable.
- **Skepticism gates:** vibe-coded dashboards can silently lie (stale data, wrong join, cheerful green while the job is dead) — the Sep 20–30 stall would have shown a *frozen* dashboard only if something kept re-rendering it; if the renderer itself is inside the stalled run, you're blind anyway. A dashboard generated *by the run that fails* dies with it; external watchdogs still matter. No repo, no example beyond a screenshot, truncated method.
